records.name: Antibody
records.tldr: A typical IgG antibody has antigen-binding arms and a stem that can interact with other parts of the immune system. Binding alone does not specify its function.
records.summary: A typical IgG has two antigen-binding arms; receptor binding and cross-reactivity depend on the particular molecule and test system, while its stem (the Fc region) can recruit immune cells and complement or extend the antibody's life in the blood. Therapeutic antibodies block growth receptors (trastuzumab on HER2, cetuximab on EGFR), release the brakes on T cells (pembrolizumab on PD-1), flag cancer cells for immune killing (rituximab on CD20), or serve as the targeting vehicle of ADCs and radioimmunotherapy. Bispecific formats have two binding specificities. Some are designed to bring a T cell and a target cell together; their structures and functions vary. Fab, the arm with the binding site, and Fc, the stem, are separate parts: binding does not guarantee killing, and Fc effector contacts need compatible effector cells or complement. Antibodies that bind the same target can act differently: a blocking antibody, an antibody-drug conjugate and a bispecific format can share a target and still differ in what follows.

records.name: Basal-like breast cancer
records.tldr: Basal-like describes a breast-cancer gene-expression pattern. It overlaps with receptor-defined triple-negative disease, but the labels use different measurements and are not interchangeable.
records.summary: Perou and colleagues profiled 65 surgical specimens from 42 patients on cDNA microarrays of 8,102 genes and found the tumours could be classified into subtypes distinguished by pervasive differences in gene expression, the origin of the intrinsic subtypes luminal A, luminal B, HER2-enriched, basal-like and normal-like (Perou 2000). The Cancer Genome Atlas integrated copy number, methylation, exome, mRNA, microRNA and protein data across primary breast cancers, confirmed four main classes, found TP53, PIK3CA and GATA3 the only genes mutated in more than 10 percent overall, and showed basal-like tumours share many molecular features with high-grade serous ovarian cancer, implying a related aetiology and similar therapeutic opportunities (TCGA 2012). Triple-negative and basal-like overlap but are not identical: of 412 triple-negative tumours 21.4 percent were non-basal-like, and of 473 basal-like tumours 31.5 percent were not triple-negative; triple-negative tumours classified as luminal or HER2-enriched had expression profiles indistinguishable from their non-triple-negative counterparts, most HER2-enriched triple-negative tumours lacked HER2 amplification, and the authors suggest triple-negative trials stratify by basal-like versus non-basal-like expression (Prat 2013). In the population-based Carolina Breast Cancer Study, using immunohistochemical surrogates (ER, PR and HER2 negative with cytokeratin 5/6 or HER1 positive), basal-like tumours were found in 39 percent of premenopausal African American women against 14 percent of postmenopausal African American and 16 percent of non-African American women; they had more TP53 mutations (44 against 15 percent), higher mitotic index and grade, and among the shortest breast cancer-specific survival (Carey 2006). Basal-like cancers are the typical cancer of BRCA1 carriers, and adenoid cystic carcinoma is a special type of basal-like tumour with an excellent outlook (Ghabach 2010), a reminder that an expression label does not establish a uniform behaviour or exact cell ancestry. PAM50 basal-like and Lehmann BL1/BL2 belong to different classifiers; a PAM50 basal-like call does not by itself assign either Lehmann profile.

notes: A research expression label, a receptor-test classification, a histological type and an inherited-risk result describe different observations. Keep the specimen, classifier/version, preprocessing, reference data and uncertainty. A label or pathway-enrichment pattern alone does not establish functional dependence or benefit from a particular treatment.

A normal-like or basal-like classifier output is not a diagnosis of benign tissue or proof of origin in a mature basal cell. The research classifier, receptor tests and histology remain separately interpretable.

Basal-marker immunohistochemistry provides contextual protein evidence, not a stand-alone subtype from ribonucleic acid (RNA) or an exact lineage trace. SOX10 is the gene symbol for SRY-box transcription factor 10; the encoded protein is a transcription factor whose tissue assay commonly assesses nuclear signal. CK5/6 denotes cytokeratins 5 and 6, epithelial structural proteins, while EGFR means epidermal growth factor receptor and is also called HER1. Nielsen and colleagues evaluated an ER, HER2, CK5/6 and EGFR protein surrogate against expression-defined basal-like cancers and in a historical tissue series. A specified research panel is not equivalent to one marker reproducing a full RNA classifier.

Cimino-Mathews and colleagues found SOX10 nuclear staining in normal myoepithelial cells and in a subset of selected triple-negative and metaplastic breast carcinomas. Their series had 100 invasive cancers, with 38 of 58 basal-like, unclassified TNBC or metaplastic cases staining, compared with two of 42 luminal/HER2 cases. These selected-series frequencies are not universal prevalence or diagnostic sensitivity. SOX10 also occurs in other tumours, including melanoma and peripheral nerve-sheath tumours. Positive staining alone does not prove breast origin, and a negative result does not exclude breast carcinoma.

Ask which cells carry the signal before interpreting a stain. Two fictional sketches can show SOX10-positive nuclei in benign myoepithelial cells around a duct and in a separate malignant-cell region. They are illustrations, not micrographs, positivity cutoffs or proof from anatomy alone. In a fictional axillary SOX10-positive mass, identify the intended cells and localisation, morphology, other markers and clinical context before assigning an origin. SOX10 does not by itself establish breast origin, basal-like RNA, Lehmann BL1, ancestry, treatment dependence or vaccine benefit.

A stain report needs the tissue/lesion and selected cells, fixation, antibody and protocol, nuclear or other expected localisation, scoring rule, presence, intensity and percentage among the intended cells. Appropriate positive and negative controls, including interpretable internal tissue controls, are needed. Preservation, scant tumour, background and staining of neighbouring benign cells can limit interpretation. Protein presence is not direct transcription-factor activity, an RNA classifier, lineage tracing or a drug-response assay. The percentage of stained tumour cells is not the probability that a treatment will work. Associations with outcome in a tissue cohort do not establish added benefit from a treatment.

records.name: Biopsy
records.tldr: Taking a small piece of the suspicious tissue so a pathologist can examine it under the microscope. It is the only way to confirm a cancer diagnosis and to learn its type and markers.
records.summary: Biopsies range from a fine needle drawing up cells, to a core needle removing a sliver of tissue, to surgical removal of the whole lesion; the sample is fixed, sliced, stained and read by a pathologist, and today also tested for protein markers and sequenced for mutations. Tissue is precious and finite, and a single biopsy samples one spot of a tumour that may vary from place to place and change over time, which is why repeat biopsies at progression and blood-based liquid biopsies have become important. Biopsies carry small risks (bleeding, infection, rarely tumour seeding) and some sites, such as the pancreas or brain, are hard to reach.

notes: Read a pathology report as an interpretation of a particular specimen. Keep the sampled site, collection date, preparation and method with the finding, and distinguish collection from the date the report became available. An addendum testing old material still describes that old specimen. The final diagnosis integrates the findings; an isolated descriptive word should not replace that interpretation. Pending, qualified or uninterpretable results retain those limits rather than becoming negative findings.

In a fictional pretreatment breast core, high-grade invasive carcinoma and completed triple-negative receptor tests answer different questions. Neither establishes a particular RNA-expression subtype or distant spread. A suspicious regional node that was not sampled is not a signed positive-node pathology finding. If later surgery finds sparse residual invasive carcinoma after treatment, preserve both the original biopsy and the later specimen, with their separate dates and settings; do not turn the first into a post-treatment measurement.

A useful report card keeps microscopic appearance and grade, individual receptor tests, anatomical extent and specimen timing in separate fields. Blank boxes in a teaching illustration contain no patient findings and calculate no stage or forecast. Ask which specimen, date, method and question each label belongs to before combining it with another observation. A small region cannot survey every part of a heterogeneous tumour, and cancer cells, immune cells, supporting tissue and treatment-related changes can coexist in the sample.

records.name: The cancer-immunity cycle
records.tldr: The cancer-immunity cycle maps linked steps from available tumour antigens to T-cell recognition and killing. It helps locate a question or bottleneck; a result at one step does not establish the whole response.
records.summary:
Chen and Mellman’s 2013 framework describes seven linked steps: release of cancer antigens; their collection and presentation; T-cell priming and activation; trafficking; entry into tumour tissue; recognition of cancer cells; and killing. Further antigen release may support another round. In conventional T-cell recognition, a displayed peptide-HLA complex and a suitable T-cell receptor are separate dependencies.

This is a T-cell-centred organizing model, not a universal route, assay result or treatment-selection algorithm. Steps overlap, priming may occur away from the tumour, and other immune mechanisms require their own account. Checkpoints and local tissue conditions affect several steps. Vaccines aim to generate or expand reactive responses, checkpoint drugs interrupt selected inhibitory signals, and engineered cells provide a recognition system and effectors. Each still needs appropriate targets, access, function and safety evidence.

notes: In a fictional vaccine study, blood cells release a cytokine after added-peptide stimulation. This supports reactivity under that assay’s conditions. Added peptide can bypass natural processing, and the result does not establish entry into the sampled tumour, recognition of naturally presenting cancer cells, useful killing or clinical benefit. Antigen release is not priming, blood expansion is not infiltration, and a return arrow does not demonstrate durable protection.

Use the cycle to name the measured step and the next untested dependency. A proposed bottleneck or complementary pair of mechanisms does not establish a beneficial or safe combination. Increasing a response can also affect healthy tissue; the model does not identify a safe intervention by itself.

For a coding change to supply a conventional T-cell target, its information must be expressed, protein produced and processed into a fragment, that peptide displayed with HLA, and a suitable receptor able to recognise the display. DNA, RNA, protein, recovered displayed peptide and controlled recognition are separate observations. A prediction at one step does not measure all the others. This conventional alpha-beta route does not describe every T cell, antibody or natural killer recognition system.

An immune observation suggests a question ladder: identify the cells and their location; ask whether a proposed peptide is produced and displayed; test recognition against appropriate target and background controls; distinguish tissue entry from useful target-specific function; then seek clinical comparisons for benefit and harm. Poor display, few matching cells, failed tissue access and impaired local function are different proposed failures. A count, supplied-peptide response or plausible pathway alone cannot complete that chain. These are task-dependent interpretation questions, not a mandatory clinical test menu.
records.analogy: A relay helps organize the questions: material must be available, presented, recognized and acted on. Several dependencies can be impaired together, and improving one handoff does not establish completion of the response. The map does not predict which treatment will help an individual.
interventions: Radiation, chemotherapy, viruses and antibody-drug conjugates can cause cancer-cell death. Antigen release alone does not establish immunogenic cell death or a useful T-cell response.
Vaccines and antigen-presenting-cell approaches investigate antigen presentation and priming. The framework locates proposed jobs; it does not establish that a particular intervention completes them.
Vascular, chemokine and stromal interventions investigate trafficking or tissue entry in defined systems. Model-specific findings do not establish a general conversion of excluded tumours.

Receptor-engineered cells and engagers change recognition requirements but still depend on accessible targets and functional cells. Conventional TCR recognition remains peptide-HLA-dependent; checkpoint blockade addresses selected inhibitory signals rather than every step.

records.name: Stage
records.tldr: Stage describes a cancer’s extent under the applicable staging system. Some breast stage groups also incorporate grade and biomarkers; stage alone does not determine an individual outcome.
records.summary: Staging describes the primary tumour, regional nodes and distant disease under cancer-specific rules. In breast cancer, clinical prognostic assessment uses history, examination, imaging and biopsy findings; surgery-first pathological prognostic assessment adds the surgical findings. Breast prognostic groups incorporate grade and biomarkers alongside TNM, so an anatomical category and a prognostic group are different descriptions. Keep the system, edition, evidence and treatment moment attached rather than applying one universal stage-to-treatment rule.

notes: Breast stage III concerns regional or locally advanced disease, whereas stage IV denotes distant spread. A high-grade invasive core does not establish either whole-body extent or a certain prognosis. Record the original diagnostic assessment and later residual or recurrent findings separately; a later report does not erase what the earlier specimen showed.

records.name: Cell cycle
records.tldr: Cells preparing to divide pass through regulated stages for growth, DNA copying and chromosome separation. Some cells remain functional while outside that cycle.
records.summary: G1 prepares the cell, S copies DNA, and G2 precedes the mitotic phase. Mitosis separates nuclear chromosomes; cytokinesis separates cytoplasm into daughter cells. G0 describes a noncycling state, which need not mean death or loss of function. Cyclins, CDKs and checkpoints regulate transitions, and their alteration can contribute to cancer without making every checkpoint absent or guaranteeing error-free division. Cell-cycle checkpoints and immune checkpoints describe different biological processes.

records.name: Chemotherapy
records.tldr: Chemotherapy uses medicines to kill cancer cells or stop their growth. Different medicines disturb different cell processes, and their benefits and harms depend on the treatment and setting.
records.summary:
Here chemotherapy means conventional cytotoxic medicines, although the word is sometimes used more broadly for cancer drug treatment. These medicines can affect DNA, RNA, the supply of building blocks or microtubules. Many of those processes also operate in healthy cells. Fast division alone does not predict response, and DNA damage alone does not describe the whole family.

A medicine, the way it is formulated, the amount and timing, and the disease setting all matter. An antibody-drug conjugate changes how a cargo is delivered and released; it does not make the cargo harmless to every healthy tissue. Some cargoes or related medicines have also been used outside conjugates.

notes: The families disturb different jobs. Taxanes such as paclitaxel suppress microtubule dynamics; vinca medicines, eribulin and some conjugate cargoes inhibit assembly or growth instead. Platinum medicines form DNA attachments and cross-links. Classic alkylating agents such as cyclophosphamide act through reactive metabolites that attach groups to DNA. Anthracyclines such as doxorubicin can stabilise topoisomerase II cutting complexes. Fluoropyrimidines such as fluorouracil interfere with nucleotide supply and RNA function. Camptothecin-class medicines such as irinotecan and topotecan trap topoisomerase I complexes. These are mechanism examples, not interchangeable doses or a ranking of benefit.

Follow a defined exposure through a drug-specific disturbance, the damage and cell response, and then recovery or death. Record the exact medicine or active metabolite, concentration and units, exposure time, whether it was removed, and the recovery period. A clinical amount in milligrams or milligrams per square metre is not a concentration at every tumour cell. Cell counts, DNA synthesis, damage markers, survival and regrowth answer different questions. A lower metabolic signal alone can reflect changed cell number or state and does not distinguish arrest from death. Use matched untreated or vehicle controls, relevant normal cells and a time course before interpreting an effect as selective killing.

In a fictional assay, Drug A reduces survival in two tumour populations after the same exposure, but one recovers more readily after drug removal; Drug B gives a separate pattern. This does not identify which population a person has, whether a tolerable exposure reaches it, or whether treatment improves an outcome. In another fictional assay there are half as many cells at the end, but no death measurement or observation after drug removal. Slower growth remains an explanation. Compare starting counts, timed death measurements and recovery to distinguish slower growth from killing; neither assay proves a cure.

NCI describes several treatment purposes: cure, reducing the chance of recurrence, stopping or slowing growth, and easing symptoms. Chemotherapy can shrink disease before surgery or radiotherapy, treat cells remaining after local treatment, help another treatment, or treat returned or spread disease. Which purpose has clinical evidence depends on the named cancer, stage, regimen, comparator, endpoint and follow-up. A cell-mechanism diagram cannot establish that evidence.

An oral medicine can still have systemic harms; an infusion is a route, not a mechanism. Side effects do not measure how well a tumour is responding, and shrinkage is different from duration of control or survival. Uptake, activation, removal, repair and cell state can differ between tumour populations. Failure of one cytotoxic medicine does not establish failure of every member, and a new product name does not establish that resistance has been bypassed. A scheduled rest interval allows recovery but does not show that every biological effect has ended.

records.name: Hot vs cold tumours
records.tldr: Hot, excluded and desert describe where specified immune cells were found in sampled tissue. Their location alone does not establish tumour recognition, effective killing or benefit from a particular drug.
records.summary:
An inflamed or hot pattern has specified immune cells within sampled tumour regions. In an excluded pattern, cells concentrate in surrounding stroma or at a boundary with less entry into malignant nests. A desert has few relevant cells in the examined regions. Cold is used for desert alone or for both desert and excluded patterns, so state the definition. A macrophage-rich sample is not automatically T-cell inflamed.

These are observations about identity and location. Some infiltrating T cells recognize viral or other non-cancer antigens; others restrain responses. Region, specimen, disease site and sampling time matter, and treatment can change the pattern. Neither a small biopsy nor a pattern label describes every site in a person or selects an immunotherapy. Exclusion suggests questions about recruitment, vessels, matrix and local cells, rather than proving one causal wall.

Equal counts can conceal different locations. Routine pathology can score a defined infiltrate, multiplex imaging adds selected cell identities and coordinates, and mixed-tissue gene expression describes programmes without directly retaining each cell’s location. Report the preparation, section, sampled regions, staining and cell-assignment rules, regional variation, output and denominator. Descriptive labels, cells per area and method-defined stromal scores are different outputs. Sectioning and staining use finite tissue. Damage, staining error, incorrect boundaries and an unrepresentative region can limit the result. A research classifier needs separate validation for a clinical selection use.

In Loi’s pooled analysis of 2,148 early TNBC patients given anthracycline-based adjuvant chemotherapy with or without taxanes, each 10 percentage-point increase in stromal TILs was associated with iDFS HR 0.87 and OS HR 0.84. This is prognosis in that population, not proof of additional checkpoint-drug benefit by hot/cold category. Taube’s tissue study also supports coexistence of lymphocyte infiltration and induced inhibitory PD-L1; hot does not mean every later immune step succeeds.

Pancreatic examples have specific settings. Feig’s pancreatic mouse model connected FAP-positive fibroblast CXCL12 with T-cell exclusion; Yamamoto’s work identified autophagy-dependent class-I degradation and tested immune rescue in mice. These are not measurements of every human pancreatic tumour. Royal’s 27-person ipilimumab study reported no RECIST responses but one delayed regression after initial progression. O’Reilly’s 65-person metastatic study reported objective response rates of 3.1% with durvalumab plus tremelimumab and 0% with durvalumab alone, without meeting its expansion threshold. These historical studies do not establish a complete treatment-selection rule or prove that one molecular subgroup is the only possible responder population.

records.name: Controlled perturbation experiment
records.tldr: A controlled perturbation changes one defined factor in an experiment and compares the response with control conditions, so that the change can be told apart from background, carrier effects and assay failure.
records.summary: A controlled perturbation deliberately changes a defined factor and measures the response against appropriate comparison conditions. Vehicle, positive, negative and mechanism controls answer different questions. A reproducible response can support an experimental claim without establishing its proposed mechanism or patient benefit. Baseline growth, timing, dose and the actual unit assigned to treatment matter.

notes: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

Keep what changed, the comparator, concentration or dose range, timing, assignment, readout and units, sample identities, replicate structure and variability. Repeated wells address variation under their preparation and allocation; independently obtained biological samples address another source of variation. Many wells from one tumour do not become independent patients, and repetition or a small p-value does not repair a missing comparison. A two-drug experiment needs vehicle, both single drugs and the combination. A larger combination effect than either single drug is not automatically synergy; that claim needs a stated reference model.

Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

records.name: ctDNA and imaging discordance
records.tldr: A blood DNA result and an imaging result can seem to disagree because they sample different material, regions, times and signals. A mismatch is a question to resolve, not a verdict on either test.
records.summary:
A circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) assay looks for tumour-associated features in a finite sample of cell-free DNA. How much tumour DNA reaches the sampled blood varies between lesions, and recovery, background DNA, the features tracked and the assay's detection limit all shape the call. Imaging measures a defined region through a physical signal. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the breast can report contrast enhancement or the volume of enhancing tissue, which is not a direct count of viable cancer cells. The two tests can therefore differ without either being wrong, and neither automatically replaces the other.

They can also share information. In Magbanua and colleagues' pilot of 84 women having neoadjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer, ctDNA concentration was correlated with MRI functional tumour volume at all four time points, with Spearman correlations of 0.42 to 0.49, and patients with detectable ctDNA had a higher median volume. Agreement was partial, and adding ctDNA early in treatment to volume-based prediction of pathological complete response gave only a numerical gain that was not statistically significant. ctDNA positivity after treatment added significantly to volume for predicting distant recurrence and death. A mismatch calls for checking dates, assay limits, the imaged region and the exact finding. It does not by itself show a false test or hidden metastatic disease.

notes: Method card, what is compared: a sampled molecular signal in plasma and a regional physical signal from a named imaging protocol. Their units, dates and thresholds stay separate, and the comparison is only as good as the date alignment of the two acquisitions.

Table, blood side: input is a blood draw and the plasma and recovered DNA analysed, and testing consumes an aliquot. Output is a qualifying call plus a defined concentration or fraction, read with the assay's detection and quantitation rules. Failure modes are low shedding, finite input, poor recovery and background or blood-cell variants.

Table, imaging side: input is the imaged region and a protocol, and contrast or tracer use depends on the modality. Output is size, volume, uptake or a qualitative finding read against protocol-specific response criteria. Failure modes are artefacts, non-tumour contributions to the signal and technique that differs between visits.

Table, what each cannot tell: blood alone cannot locate a lesion or give a cell count. Imaging alone cannot count viable tumour cells, and enhancement can have more than one tissue cause. Neither agreement nor disagreement shows that a treatment change would help, which is a clinical-utility question.

Evidence read: Magbanua's pilot (84 patients, MTM/mL against MRI functional tumour volume) found correlation at T0 to T3 with rho 0.49, 0.42, 0.42 and 0.43, and its authors call the findings preliminary in a limited cohort needing larger validation. It supports partial agreement and does not set a rule for redirecting treatment.

Interpretation rule, from finite sampling: a plasma aliquot can hold no tumour molecule when the true share is small, so no qualifying ctDNA signal alongside an abnormal MRI region does not show the region is only scar. The converse holds too: a clear image does not exclude tumour DNA in blood. Each result answers only its own question.

Source attribution comes first: a positive plasma variant may come from a blood-cell clone rather than a tumour. In Razavi's paired sequencing, 53.2% of cell-free DNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 people without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis, so a discordant positive needs origin checks before it is read as occult disease.

Half-life, scoped: Diehl and colleagues estimated a ctDNA half-life after surgery of 114 minutes by evaluating one subject whose plasma was sampled at several early times after complete resection in a study of 162 plasma samples from 18 subjects with colorectal cancer (Diehl 2008). That is a single-subject estimate of post-resection clearance in colorectal cancer, not a universal cfDNA half-life, a breast-cancer figure or a blood-draw schedule. DNA release and clearance can change sooner than visible tissue structure, which is a reason to align the dates of the blood and imaging acquisitions.

Use the blood collection date and imaging acquisition date to compare biology, then keep the reporting dates as a separate measure of when the information became available. Imaging does not remove a tissue aliquot for molecular analysis; contrast or tracer use belongs to the specific protocol. Agreement can reflect shared dependence on disease burden and is not two independent proofs of the same mechanism. Combining measurements into a decision rule needs validation of the combination and its intended outcome.

In a fictional early-breast-cancer example, a negative plasma result is not an examination of the breast tumour bed or regional nodes. It cannot by itself establish pathological complete response or validate skipping surgery. Using a result to remove a treatment needs evidence for that decision strategy and its clinical outcomes, beyond showing that an assay can detect a signal. This is an interpretation limit, not a claim that no omission study exists.

records.name: ER status (oestrogen receptor by IHC)
records.tldr: ER status reports oestrogen-receptor staining in tumour-cell nuclei. In invasive breast cancer, at least 1% is positive; 1% to 10% is ER-low positive, with limited evidence about endocrine-treatment benefit.
records.summary:
The oestrogen receptor is an intracellular protein involved in responses to oestrogen and regulation of gene expression. A clinical ER result measures receptor staining in identified tumour-cell nuclei, not the amount of oestrogen in blood or every downstream signal.

The ASCO/CAP invasive-breast guideline uses validated immunohistochemistry: at least 1% stained tumour-cell nuclei is positive, below 1% is negative, and 1% to 10% is reported as ER-low positive. These cancers are heterogeneous and can have features resembling ER-negative disease, but they remain ER-positive. Limited evidence suggests possible endocrine benefit, so the category supports consideration of endocrine treatment rather than a guaranteed response or a treatment mandate.

notes: Receptor presence is like having machinery able to receive a message; it does not show equal signalling in every cell or equal drug sensitivity. Oestrogen binding can influence gene programmes, while endocrine treatments interfere with hormone production or action. This differs from menopausal hormone replacement. ER is not the same observation as the cell-surface HER2 receptor, and clinical nuclear staining is not a statement that the protein can exist only in that location.

The measurement route is tissue, identification of invasive tumour cells, a validated nuclear stain, review of controls, percentage and intensity, then interpretation. Keep the specimen/block and collection context; IHC uses tissue sections. Percentage counts positive nuclei among the intended tumour cells, while intensity describes stain strength. Poor preservation, artefact or failed controls can prevent interpretation: uninterpretable does not mean negative. A bulk RNA result does not replace validated clinical IHC. ASCO/CAP recommends ER testing in DCIS to assess potential endocrine risk reduction, with PR optional there; invasive and in-situ contexts should be stated.

For a fictional invasive tumour with adequate controls, ER staining in 4% of tumour-cell nuclei is ER-low positive. It is not 4% predicted treatment benefit and is not rounded down to ER-negative because an RNA classifier says basal-like. Preserve the stain denominator, intensity and category alongside that separate expression result. If controls fail, resolve the testing problem before assigning a negative category. ER and PR results remain separate observations.

records.name: Gamma-delta T cells
records.tldr: Gamma-delta T cells are a family of T cells whose receptor is built from different protein chains than most T cells, and different subsets recognise different signals, often without the usual peptide display. The family name does not say which signal a particular cell, or an engineered product, uses to find a tumour.
records.summary: The T-cell receptor of most T cells has alpha and beta chains; gamma-delta T cells have gamma and delta chains and also carry other activating and inhibitory receptors. They remain T cells and are distinct from natural killer cells. A review distinguishes gamma-delta from alpha-beta T cells partly by the antigens their receptors recognise, and notes that NKG2D is expressed by many gamma-delta subsets as well as by natural killer cells and CD8 T cells (Vantourout and Hayday, 2013). Names such as Vδ1 and Vγ9Vδ2 describe receptor variable regions and mark subsets that sit in different places. Healthy human breast tissue harboured a distinct gamma-delta compartment made mainly of Vδ1 cells, whereas Vδ2 cells predominate in blood; the breast Vδ1 cells could be activated innately through the NKG2D receptor, and in paired samples from 11 people with triple-negative breast cancer, progression-free and overall survival correlated with Vδ1 representation but not with total gamma-delta or Vδ2 cells (Wu et al., 2019). That is a small observational association in tissue biology and did not test an infused product.

notes: Recognition differs by subset, and it is not always free of HLA. For the Vγ9Vδ2 subset, which responds to phosphoantigens (small phosphorylated metabolites produced by microbes and overexpressed by some cancers), butyrophilin 2A1 (BTN2A1) binds the Vγ9 chain of the receptor, associates with a second butyrophilin, BTN3A1, and the two act together to start the response; a second ligand, possibly BTN3A1, binds a separate region that includes the Vδ2 chain (Rigau et al., 2020). This is not a peptide sitting in an HLA groove. HLA independence is also not universal: one characterised Vγ5Vδ1 receptor was restricted by HLA-A*24:02 and depended on the CD8-alpha co-receptor, acting on blood-cancer and solid-tumour cells in vitro and in vivo while sparing healthy tissue in those models (Kierkels et al., 2019). That receptor's mechanism is not an eligibility rule for the family.

An engineered receptor is a separate recognition route. Adding a GD2-directed chimeric antigen receptor to expanded human Vδ1 and Vδ2 cells increased GD2-specific killing of GD2-expressing cancer cell lines, did not impair movement towards tumour cells in vitro, and expanded Vδ2 cells kept the ability to take up tumour antigen and cross-present it to alpha-beta T cells (Capsomidis et al., 2018). That is a preclinical result for that preparation, and it does not show that any gamma-delta product enters tumours, cross-presents usefully or prevents antigen escape in patients. An allogeneic gamma-delta product that the registry names HLA-G-CAR.BiTE allogeneic γδ T cells (NCT06150885, phase 1 and 2) was listed as recruiting when the registry record was read for this entry; the record describes the product and the study design and reports no efficacy. A receptor added to a cell needs its own target on the tumour, HLA-low does not mean target-positive, and avoiding peptide presentation is not the same as avoiding antigen escape. Cells are identified by flow cytometry and receptor sequencing, but a response against one target line does not establish tumour entry, persistence or benefit, and matched cells without the added receptor are needed to separate native from engineered recognition. Two cautions are OnCo's reasoning and not findings of the cited papers: a product made of many receptor clones is not automatically broader or more effective than one defined clone, and the name gamma-delta describes the receptor chains and not the cell source, so whether cells came from the patient or from a donor has to be stated separately.

Measurement separates identity, repertoire and function. Sanz et al. (2023) used flow cytometry to isolate human gamma-delta subsets and assessed receptor repertoires separately from cytotoxicity. Their Daudi-cell cocultures included target-only and effector-only controls; degranulation, granzyme or perforin measurements and target-cell death were distinct readouts. These are results for defined human subsets and laboratory targets, not a universal assay or a test of tumour entry in patients.

For interpretation, report the parent population, percentage and any valid absolute count with the specimen and sampling method. Receptor-sequence abundance does not identify the receptor ligand. Rigau et al. (2020) established a defined BTN2A1-dependent recognition mechanism for the Vgamma9Vdelta2 phosphoantigen response; that specificity is an example of why innate-like does not mean nonspecific. To test native versus added-receptor recognition, compare matched cells without the added receptor, target-positive and target-negative cells, and a suitable receptor-blocking or target-perturbation condition. Keep relevant healthy-cell controls, viability and exposure conditions explicit. This is experimental-design reasoning from the separate recognition mechanisms, not a claim that one cited assay validates every product. HLA loss does not establish that the native ligand or the added receptor target is present, and two recognition routes do not prove escape prevention.

records.name: Gene expression
records.tldr: Gene expression produces RNA and, for coding messages, protein. Measurements at those steps are related but do not answer the same question.
records.summary: Transcription makes RNA from DNA; translation reads a coding message in codons to make a polypeptide. This information-flow description does not require every RNA to become protein. A promoter recruits transcription machinery. Enhancers influence transcription through regulatory interactions that can span distant DNA positions. Transcription factors recognize sequence features and participate in regulation. Chromatin, RNA processing and turnover, translation, protein processing and degradation all influence the eventual product. A transcript’s frame and reference context matter when interpreting a sequence change.

records.name: Hallmarks of Cancer
records.tldr: The hallmarks organise research on cancer capabilities. The framework has changed over time and is not a diagnostic checklist or a treatment-selection test.
records.summary: The hallmarks framework groups recurring capabilities and enabling processes involved in cancer. Its 2000, 2011 and 2022 versions distinguish core capabilities from emerging or provisional additions. Different cells and their surroundings can contribute, and a measurement of one process does not establish all the others.

notes: The hallmarks are a versioned research framework, not a diagnostic checklist, stage, clinical assay standard or a demand that every cell independently perform every capability. The 2000 proposal contained six capabilities. The 2011 account retained six, added two emerging capabilities and described two enabling characteristics. In the 2022 account, the two emerging capabilities joined the eight core capabilities.

The eight core capabilities are sustained growth signalling, evasion of growth restraints, resistance to cell death, sustained replicative capacity, obtaining a blood supply, invasion and distant colonisation, altered metabolism, and evasion of immune control. These are distinct processes: division speed does not measure replicative capacity, and a growth-related gene alteration does not establish invasion or immune escape. Vascular access can include existing vessels, not only new vessel growth.

Genome instability and mutation, and tumour-promoting inflammation, are enabling characteristics in the stated framework; not every mutation matters and not all inflammation promotes cancer. Hanahan’s 2022 additions remain at different explanatory levels: plasticity as a proposed capability, nonmutational epigenetic reprogramming and microbiomes as possible enablers, and senescent cells as microenvironment participants. They are not four equivalent established core hallmarks.

Capabilities can depend on cooperation with surrounding cells. To measure one, specify the process: division, death, invasion, vascular relations, metabolism or immune function. An RNA program is not a direct measurement of every capability or metabolic flux, and there is no universal hallmark unit or cutoff selecting treatment. In a fictional mutation-rich report, an enabling characteristic alone neither establishes distant disease nor proves those mutations caused the behaviour. A framework diagram organises concepts and provisional additions; it does not measure them in a specimen.

Cancer develops when altered body cells grow outside normal controls. Invasion into neighbouring tissue and metastasis to a distant site are distinct capabilities, rather than consequences established by one report label. NCI also describes surrounding immune cells, fibroblasts, vessels and molecules as part of the tumour microenvironment. A specimen named for a cancer can therefore contain several cell populations; the name does not make every sampled cell malignant.

records.name: HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH-amplified)
records.tldr: HER2-positive breast cancer has an integrated result showing HER2 protein overexpression or gene amplification under the applicable testing rules. The result is separate from eligibility for a specific medicine.
records.summary:
Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a cell-surface receptor protein encoded by ERBB2. Gene amplification, protein abundance measured by immunohistochemistry and RNA expression are different observations. In invasive breast cancer, HER2 status integrates the IHC pattern and indicated in-situ hybridisation workup under the applicable guideline. IHC 2+ is equivocal, not half-positive or a completed negative result.

A HER2-positive result and a HER2-enriched RNA subtype are not interchangeable. HER2-low or ultralow staining remains negative for overexpression/amplification in the relevant breast context, while some specified treatment settings use low expression to select an antibody-drug conjugate. A signalling receptor can also serve as a delivery address; neither the label nor one staining category proves pathway dependence, eligibility or individual drug benefit.

records.name: Histology
records.tldr: The study of tissue under the microscope. A cancer's histology is what kind of cells it is made of and how they are arranged, which is how a pathologist names it and grades it.
records.summary: Thin slices of fixed tissue are stained, classically with haematoxylin and eosin (H&E), so that nuclei show purple and the surrounding tissue pink; the pathologist reads cell type, architecture, invasion, grade, and margins, then adds immunohistochemistry and molecular tests as needed. Histology defines the cancer's name (adenocarcinoma, squamous, small cell, sarcoma subtype) and, with stage, is the foundation of treatment; a change in histology at progression, such as an EGFR-mutant adenocarcinoma transforming into small-cell lung cancer, changes therapy entirely. Digital slide scanning and AI models now assist with grading, counting and predicting molecular features from the image alone.

records.name: Immune exclusion
records.tldr: Immune exclusion describes immune cells concentrated outside cancer-cell regions. Their distribution raises questions about access; it does not identify the barrier or a treatment that will overcome it.
records.summary:
After priming, a T cell must be recruited, adhere to and leave a vessel, traverse stroma and reach relevant cancer cells. An excluded distribution records where cells were found. It does not establish why they stopped. A cell that has reached a target but is inhibited has a different measured problem, although access and functional failures can coexist.

Candidate mechanisms include recruitment signals, vascular interactions, matrix architecture, fibroblast signalling and myeloid-cell contacts. Their evidence comes from different cancers, human tissue studies and experimental models. A location measurement, causal perturbation and successful clinical intervention are different claims. Dense stroma alone does not diagnose exclusion or identify a safe way to reverse it.

This is a defined melanoma mechanism, not a universal explanation for every excluded tissue pattern.

Mariathasan associated stromal fibroblast TGF-beta signalling, exclusion and atezolizumab non-response in metastatic urothelial cancer; combined TGF-beta and PD-L1 blockade improved penetration and regression in mice. Hammerl’s spatial analysis of 681 TNBCs distinguished excluded, ignored and inflamed groups. Excluded samples showed collagen-10 deposits and TGF-beta/VEGF programmes; ignored samples showed either dense CD163-positive myeloid cells or WNT/PPAR-gamma programmes. The classifier also associated with anti-PD-1 response in a metastatic-TNBC phase-II trial. Gruosso separately associated stroma-restricted CD8 cells and stromal PD-L1 with poorer outcome. These associations do not prove the observed barrier caused resistance or that its removal helps a particular patient.

A chemokine can matter after entry. Chow found that CXCR3 and dendritic-cell-derived CXCL9 were required for productive anti-PD-1 responses in tumour-bearing mice but were not required for initial CD8 infiltration. This is different from Mikucki’s transferred-cell vascular-trafficking experiment. Name the tested step, model, stimulus and endpoint before treating the two studies as the same claim.

Multiplex imaging can separately count CD8 cells in stroma and malignant nests and measure distances. Bulk chemokine, fibroblast or TGF-beta RNA programmes lose direct location. A high stromal TIL area score can therefore coexist with exclusion. In a fictional comparison, collagen-rich stroma with peripheral CD8 cells and high TGF-beta suggests a different access question from sparse T cells with low recruiting chemokines. Both remain hypotheses requiring appropriate measurements and functional controls, rather than diagnoses from one image.

Feig’s pancreatic mouse model found T cells outside cancer-cell regions coated with CAF-derived CXCL12; fibroblast depletion or CXCR4 blockade improved access and revealed checkpoint-antibody activity in that model. Separately, Balachandran’s human pancreatic-cancer study associated combined neoantigen and CD8 features with long survival, detected relevant T-cell reactivity and observed selective loss of high-quality neoantigenic clones during metastatic progression. Those findings do not show that every long-term survivor overcame one specific physical exclusion barrier.

records.name: Immune system
records.tldr: The body's defence network of cells and molecules that recognises and destroys infected, foreign and abnormal cells. It kills most would-be cancers before they are ever noticed; the ones that survive have learned to hide from it.
records.summary: Innate immunity uses inherited sensing systems (barriers, soluble defences such as complement, phagocytes such as macrophages and neutrophils, natural killer cells, and sensors of microbial or damage-related features), while adaptive immunity expands T cells and B cells whose diverse antigen receptors are assembled during development and selected by an encounter, with some descendants persisting as memory cells. The two cooperate: dendritic cells, cytokines and lymph nodes connect innate sensing to adaptive responses, and antibodies and T cells in turn guide innate cells.

notes: Fast and memoryless against slow and remembering is a starting tendency and not a rule: mice lacking functional T and B cells were protected against repeat Candida albicans infection in a monocyte-dependent way (Quintin et al., 2012), and natural killer cells carrying the Ly49H receptor expanded about 100-fold in the spleen after mouse cytomegalovirus infection, persisted for months and expanded again after transfer to a new host (Sun et al., 2009).

A list of cell types is a roster and not a functional report: a cell-family name does not show what a cell is doing, a marker shared by several populations is not a complete identity test (single-cell sequencing of human blood found six dendritic-cell and four monocyte subtypes; Villani et al., 2017), and a fraction of immune cells depends on its denominator (percent of recovered immune cells, of T cells and of all tissue cells are different quantities). Blood composition does not substitute for tumour composition, and a count of immune cells in a tumour does not by itself show recognition or killing. CD4 and CD8 are co-receptors and not permanent helper and killer assignments, tumour-associated macrophage names a setting, myeloid-derived suppressor cells need an operational phenotype and a test of suppressive function, and natural killer T cells are a T-cell family distinct from natural killer cells despite the name. In the classical description innate immunity is rapid and without immunologic memory while adaptive immunity is antigen-specific with a capacity for memory, and the two are not mutually exclusive (Marshall et al., 2018). Cytotoxic CD4 T cells have been found in infections, tumours and inflammatory disease, so a CD4 or CD8 label does not fix a helper or killer role (Venkatesh et al., 2023), and a myeloid-derived suppressor cell label rests on myeloid origin plus shown suppressive function (Bronte et al., 2016). CD4 and CD8 are coreceptors for T-cell receptors that recognise MHC, and a review discusses how they help impose MHC specificity during thymic selection (Van Laethem et al., 2012), so a CD4 or CD8 label names a coreceptor and not a job.

Among innate cells, phagocytes (neutrophils and macrophages) engulf and kill microbes, and natural killer cells play a major role in the rejection of tumours and the destruction of virus-infected cells through perforins and granzymes (Marshall et al., 2018). The receptor comparison concerns how recognition equipment is generated: inherited, germline-encoded receptors include Toll-like and natural killer receptors, whereas developing T and B cells assemble diverse antigen receptors by somatic V(D)J recombination (Hayday and Vantourout, 2020; Oettinger et al., 1990; Nemazee, 2017); one review describes the adaptive system as in turn activating innate effector mechanisms in an antigen-specific manner (Medzhitov, 2007).

Most adjuvants are thought to enhance T-cell and B-cell responses by engaging the innate immune system and not the lymphocytes directly (Coffman et al., 2010), so a vaccine can create an inflammatory context, and a response to an unrelated control antigen has to be measured to show that a response to the vaccine antigen is selective; in OnCo's reasoning, a manufactured antibody is also not evidence that the recipient made antibodies. Counts of cells, concentrations in picograms per millilitre and antigen-matched functional assays answer different questions, and a report should say which specimen, which time, which stimulation and which background control was used (OnCo reporting advice).

Tumours are recognised because they display mutated proteins and stress signals, but successful tumours evade destruction by displaying 'don't attack me' checkpoint signals, hiding their antigens, recruiting suppressive cells, and walling themselves off; 'avoiding immune destruction' is one of the hallmarks of cancer. Immunotherapy in its many forms (checkpoint inhibitors, engineered T cells, bispecifics, vaccines) aims to restore or engineer the immune system's ability to see and kill the tumour.

Cell-family roster, T cells: diverse antigen receptors support antigen-specific responses; functions can include help through signals, regulation and target-cell killing. A CD4 or CD8 marker is a coreceptor label, not a permanent helper or killer assignment. Interpretation: the presence of T cells does not establish which antigen they recognise or that killing is occurring (Marshall et al., 2018; Venkatesh et al., 2023).

Cell-family roster, B cells and plasma cells: B cells recognise antigen, can present it to T cells and can produce cytokine signals; plasma cells specialise in antibody secretion (Marshall et al., 2018; de Gruijter et al., 2022). Interpretation: counting either family does not identify what its antibodies bind or whether those antibodies help control a tumour.

Cell-family roster, natural killer cells: activating and inhibitory inputs together influence target-cell damage and cytokine production; these cells can release perforin, granzymes and interferon gamma (Marshall et al., 2018). Interpretation: a count of natural killer cells does not show that every abnormal cell will be attacked. The required signals, cell state and tested target still matter.

Cell-family roster, macrophages: engulfment, antigen presentation and signalling coexist with roles in tissue maintenance and repair. The repair, inflammatory and fibrotic programmes described by Wynn and Vannella (2016) depend on context. Interpretation: a macrophage count or location does not establish a universally beneficial or suppressive function.

Cell-family roster, dendritic cells: they collect and display antigen and provide signals that can shape T-cell priming, connecting innate and adaptive immunity (Marshall et al., 2018). Interpretation: their presence does not establish that the relevant antigen was displayed with the supporting signals needed for a useful response.

Cell-family roster, neutrophils: engulfment and antimicrobial activity are accompanied by inflammatory signalling and tissue effects. Afonso et al. (2012) showed cell-to-cell signal relay by leukotriene B4 in defined neutrophil chemotaxis experiments, including cells from mice with or without the formyl peptide receptor 1. Peiseler and Kubes (2019) review roles in tissue damage, resolution of inflammation and repair, including sterile injury. Interpretation: a neutrophil count alone does not diagnose infection or establish cancer promotion or cancer control.

Recognition-system comparison: innate recognition equipment is inherited; T-cell and B-cell antigen receptors are diversified and assembled during development. Exposure can change innate activation, recruitment and later responsiveness, while an adaptive response can select clones that expand, differentiate and persist as memory. Speed is a separate axis: innate responses are often early but can persist, and adaptive recall can be rapid. Mouse fungal and viral experiments demonstrate particular forms of trained monocyte or memory-like natural killer responses, not a rule that every innate response has conventional T-cell or B-cell memory (Quintin et al., 2012; Sun et al., 2009; Hayday and Vantourout, 2020). Antigen specificity alone does not establish activation or benefit.

Measurement comparison: cell counts describe a sampled population, protein concentration describes an amount per volume, and an antigen-matched functional assay describes an activity under its test conditions. Rodero et al. (2017) measured interferon-alpha protein, interferon-responsive RNA and antiviral activity as different readouts; Sanz et al. (2023) separately measured gamma-delta cell phenotype, receptor repertoire and target-cell killing. The reporting inference is to keep specimen, collection time, cell identity, stimulation, viability and background controls explicit. A concentration in picograms per millilitre is not a cell count or an antigen-specific response.

records.name: Intra-tumour heterogeneity
records.tldr: Cancer cells can differ in DNA, molecular state and behaviour across regions and time. One sample and one target measurement need not represent every population.
records.summary: Intratumour heterogeneity includes genetic branches and changing cell states, which are distinct biological axes. A locally clonal alteration may not be shared by unseen disease, and shared DNA does not guarantee uniform protein expression or therapeutic coverage. Interpretation retains the sample, method and uncertainty.

notes: Heterogeneity includes DNA differences, molecular states and behaviour across regions, lesions and time. Clones and subclones describe ancestry; clonal variants are estimated within a stated analysed cancer-cell population. A sampled ancestral trunk is not proof of presence in unseen lesions. Sequencing-read or molecule variant allele fractions differ from modelled cancer-cell fractions, which depend on purity, copy number, detection limits and ancestry assumptions.

Neftel integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, genetic analysis and experimental lineage tracing in glioblastoma to describe four main states and plasticity between them. This is not a universal state map for all cancers. An RNA cluster is not automatically a genetic clone. A population detected after therapy can reflect previously undetected cells, acquired changes or a changed state; two snapshots may not separate these explanations.

In a fictional specimen with 60 target-positive and 40 target-negative cells, perfect specificity for the target can still leave the negative population. A target-rich local biopsy is not a whole-tumour response probability. Even a shared DNA trunk does not guarantee RNA, surface protein, presented peptide or effective therapeutic coverage in every cell. A selected culture can also overrepresent cells that grow under its conditions.

If two adequately tested regions share A while B is found in only one, A is a candidate shared ancestral feature and B is branch-associated under the tested model. A third unsampled site remains unknown. Retain region, date, specimen, method, resolution and uncertainty across multiregion, single-cell, spatial and modelled-fraction studies. DNA outlines, RNA-state symbols and surface marks in a figure represent different layers; icon counts are not measured fractions or treatment-response estimates.

records.name: KEYNOTE-522
records.tldr: The trial that added immunotherapy to pre-surgery chemotherapy for triple-negative breast cancer and, uniquely, improved survival.
records.summary: 1,174 patients. pCR 64.8% vs 51.2%; event-free survival at 5 years 81.2% vs 72.2%; 7-year EFS 78.3% vs 69.8% and OS 85.1% vs 77.2% (ASCO 2026 update). Defines the standard of care for stage II-III TNBC. Open questions: whether adjuvant pembrolizumab is needed after pCR (OptimICE-pCR) and how to escalate for residual disease.

records.name: Neoadjuvant / adjuvant / perioperative
records.tldr: Neoadjuvant treatment is given before surgery, adjuvant treatment after it, and perioperative treatment around both phases. The benefit and risks of the timing depend on the disease and complete regimen.
records.summary:
Neoadjuvant, adjuvant and perioperative describe timing before surgery, after surgery or across both phases. Neoadjuvant therapy can aim to reduce disease before an operation and provides response information from treated tissue. Adjuvant therapy aims to reduce risk from disease that may remain. A pathological response and a later clinical outcome are different endpoints.

Timing comparisons need the actual population, intervention and comparator. Liu’s two mouse breast-cancer models supported testing preoperative immunotherapy, not a universal human timing rule or proof that retained tumour antigen explains every clinical result. KEYNOTE-522 assigned a complete before-and-after pembrolizumab regimen against its comparator; that design does not independently randomize the two phases and cannot isolate each phase’s contribution.

Eight planned 3-week preoperative cycles and nine postoperative cycles correspond to about 24 and 27 weeks; delays and clinical decisions can alter actual timing. The U.S. label describes tumour-size and nodal eligibility and enrolment regardless of PD-L1 expression. A stage label alone is not a personal treatment instruction. The complete regimen comparison did not independently randomise its two phases.

Neoadjuvant treatment can reduce a tumour before an operation and leave treated tissue for response assessment. Subsequent breast and nodal pathology, radiation indications and further systemic options answer separate questions. Residual disease does not automatically choose one added medicine: prior treatment, biomarker eligibility, the population actually studied and uncertainty about sequencing or combination remain relevant. A pathological response is not a survival estimate or proof that a treatment component can be omitted.

records.name: NK cell
records.tldr: Natural killer cells integrate activating and inhibitory inputs to respond to abnormal cells. An added CAR supplies another recognition route; missing self is one input rather than a guarantee of killing.
records.summary: Some inhibitory NK receptors recognize self HLA class I, while activating receptors respond to other features. Reduced self display can weaken an inhibitory input, but the NK cell, its prior education, activating signals and target context still determine the response. NK cells can also contribute antibody-dependent killing through Fc receptors. Donor-derived or engineered NK-cell products need their own compatibility, persistence and safety assessment rather than a blanket claim that matching or rejection never matters. The principle comes from mouse experiments: lymphoma cells selected for loss of H-2 were less malignant at low dose and were rejected by a non-adaptive mechanism, which suggested that natural killer cells are effectors in a defence system geared to detect reduced self MHC (Kärre et al., 1986); that does not guarantee the same outcome for any human tumour. MHC class I molecules are ligands for killer-cell immunoglobulin-like receptors (Parham, 2005): two-domain KIR2D receptors bind HLA-C alleles and three-domain KIR3D receptors bind HLA-A and HLA-B alleles, and the KIR family includes activating as well as inhibitory members (Mariuzza et al., 2025). CD94/NKG2A binds HLA-E, and HLA-E surface expression was enough to protect target cells from lysis by CD94/NKG2A-positive NK clones (Braud et al., 1998). NKG2D binds class I-related proteins including MICA, MICB and ULBP1 to 3 (Mariuzza et al., 2025), and engagement of NKG2D activated NK and gamma-delta T-cell cytolysis against epithelial tumour cells expressing MICA (Bauer et al., 1999). No single activating receptor dominates, since NK cells integrate synergistic signals from several (Long et al., 2013), and responsiveness depends on prior education: in human cell experiments, cytokine stimulation let hyporesponsive NK cells acquire KIR and function when the cognate MHC was present (Juelke et al., 2009). Loss of one HLA allele is not loss of all class I. Loss of beta-2 microglobulin removed surface class I in one of four relapsing melanoma patients (Zaretsky et al., 2016), and because HLA-E is assembled with beta-2 microglobulin, the KIR and NKG2A restraints would be expected to lift together; that last step is an inference not tested in the cited abstracts. A flow-based cytotoxicity assay that stains target and effector nuclei separately and distinguishes live from dead nuclei has been validated with NK-92 cells, CAR-T cells and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (Rabinovich et al., 2019). Target death is not a count of effector cells that released granule contents: surface CD107a marked NK cells that degranulated after stimulation with MHC-devoid targets and correlated with lysis, and also marked a large subset that did not secrete cytokine, so different readouts count different cells (Alter et al., 2004). CD16 is a low-affinity Fc receptor for IgG that mediates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity by NK cells (Liu, 2022), a route separate from missing-self recognition. Neither assay readout shows tumour entry or clinical benefit.

notes: The original missing-self experiment compared mouse lymphoma variants with reduced H-2 expression in defined hosts. It supports an immune-recognition principle, not a universal rule that every HLA-low human tumor is killed by every NK product.

A CAR, native NK receptors and cytokine support provide different inputs. The cord-blood product in Liu combined all of these design layers; a favorable observation for that construct does not isolate the CAR contribution or establish the same behavior for NK-92, donor blood or pluripotent-cell-derived preparations. NK and NKT cells are different cell families.

The receptor-level map separates inhibitory KIR/HLA and NKG2A/HLA-E interactions from activating stress-ligand and antibody-Fc inputs. Receptor proteins, genotype, ligand expression, degranulation and controlled target killing are different readouts. A loss of inhibitory display without adequate activating input does not guarantee killing, and a perioperative blood NK measurement does not describe every residual-disease site.

records.name: Pathologic complete response (pCR)
records.tldr: Pathological complete response records the absence of specified residual cancer in tissue after preoperative treatment. The specimen and response definition must accompany the result.
records.summary: In breast cancer, pCR must retain its named definition and specimens. FDA trial guidance describes two combined breast-and-sampled-node endpoints after neoadjuvant treatment: one permits residual ductal carcinoma in situ and the other excludes it. Older studies have also used breast-only definitions, so their response rates cannot be assumed to describe the combined endpoint. Response in sampled tissue, margin status, imaging, blood tests and long-term outcomes answer different questions.

notes: In FDA breast-trial guidance, ypT0/Tis ypN0 means no residual invasive cancer on haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) examination of the complete resected breast specimen and all sampled regional nodes after neoadjuvant systemic treatment. Residual DCIS is permitted. The stricter ypT0 ypN0 definition also excludes in situ cancer. Preserve the actual protocol and nodal assessment rules.

Breast-only clearance is not the combined breast-and-node endpoint. Residual invasive cancer in a sampled node prevents that combined pCR result even when breast invasion is absent or a blood assay is negative. A small negative biopsy, imaging response and negative circulating tumour DNA are different observations.

Residual DCIS can meet the invasive-clearance definition while still requiring separate margin assessment. In an otherwise qualifying specimen with DCIS but no breast invasion and no residual sampled-node cancer, the permissive definition is met and the stricter one is not. Neither pCR nor a negative local edge certifies cure or absence at every body site.

Cortazar and colleagues' CTNeoBC analysis pooled 11955 patients from 12 trials. In triple-negative disease, attaining ypT0/is ypN0 was associated with event-free-survival HR 0.24 and overall-survival HR 0.16 versus not attaining pCR. This patient-level association is not a guaranteed personal outcome.

Trial-level increases in pCR had little association with event-free or overall-survival effects in CTNeoBC (R squared 0.03 and 0.24 respectively). The analysis could not validate pCR as a surrogate for improved long-term outcomes. A study reporting a pCR gain without mature survival comparison cannot infer the size of a survival benefit from the responder association.

FDA's July 2020 revision 1 guidance concerns pCR endpoints for trial design and accelerated approval in high-risk early-stage breast cancer. It is not an individual treatment or cure rule. In the notation, y denotes assessment after neoadjuvant treatment and p denotes pathological assessment. Sections and stains consume finite tissue; incomplete sampling, unexamined nodes and mixed endpoint definitions can invalidate comparisons.

KEYNOTE-522 separately demonstrated endpoint and survival results for the whole perioperative regimen in previously untreated stage II or III TNBC. In the 2020 primary pCR analysis of the first 602 randomised participants, pembrolizumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy yielded 64.8% pCR versus 51.2% with placebo plus chemotherapy (difference 13.6 percentage points, 95% CI 5.4 to 21.8). The final 2024 overall-survival report covered all 1,174 randomised participants, including postoperative pembrolizumab or placebo: at 60 months, overall survival was 86.6% versus 81.7% (P = 0.002; median follow-up 75.1 months). Survival was measured directly; the pCR gain did not mathematically predict it or isolate which perioperative component produced the benefit.

In fictional case A, no breast invasion, residual DCIS and no residual cancer in sampled nodes meet ypT0/Tis ypN0 but not ypT0 ypN0. In fictional case B, the same breast finding plus a 4-mm residual invasive nodal deposit meets neither combined endpoint. Identical DCIS-at-ink findings in either case remain a separate margin question.

Subtract within the same endpoint and analysis: 64.8 minus 51.2 gives a 13.6-percentage-point pCR difference in the first 602 participants; 86.6 minus 81.7 gives 4.9 points in the separately reported 60-month survival estimates for all 1,174. The latter is often rounded to about five more people alive per hundred under the trial comparison. These time-to-event estimates are not literal counts from a complete hundred-person group, an individual forecast or a conversion from the pCR difference.

Triple-negative disease is where pathological complete response means most: in the CTNeoBC pooled analysis of 11,955 patients, eradication of tumour from breast and nodes (ypT0/is ypN0) was associated with event-free survival hazard ratio 0.24 and overall survival 0.16 in triple-negative disease, the strongest association of any subtype, yet trial-level increases in the rate did not predict survival gains (Cortazar 2014).

Triple-negative patients reach a complete response more often than others (22 against 11 percent in the MD Anderson series, 1985 to 2004) and then have similar survival, while those with residual disease do worse, particularly in the first three years (Liedtke 2008). Adding pembrolizumab to platinum chemotherapy raised the rate from 51.2 to 64.8 percent in KEYNOTE-522 (Schmid 2020).

records.name: PD-1
records.tldr: PD-1 helps regulate T-cell responses. Blocking its signals can improve cancer control in studied settings, but it does not guarantee recognition, killing or benefit.
records.summary: PD-1 blockade (pembrolizumab, nivolumab, cemiplimab, dostarlimab and a growing list of biosimilar-adjacent agents) is standard across melanoma, NSCLC, RCC, urothelial, head and neck, MSI-high tumours, TNBC (with chemotherapy), Hodgkin lymphoma, and more. PD-1×VEGF bispecifics (ivonescimab) and PD-1×CTLA-4 combinations are the next wave.

records.name: Pembrolizumab
records.tldr: Pembrolizumab is a PD-1 blocking antibody approved in more than 40 settings, from melanoma and lung cancer to the first tumour-agnostic approval for mismatch-repair-deficient tumours in 2017, and before and after surgery in triple-negative breast cancer. A subcutaneous form arrived in 2025, and it is the backbone partner for ADCs and personalised neoantigen vaccines.

records.name: PR status (progesterone receptor by IHC)
records.tldr: PR status measures progesterone-receptor staining in tumour-cell nuclei. It is reported separately from ER and is primarily prognostic in ER-positive invasive breast cancer.
records.summary:
The progesterone receptor is an intracellular hormone-response protein. Its tissue stain does not measure circulating progesterone or every interaction with ER signalling. In invasive breast cancer, the ASCO/CAP guideline uses at least 1% positive tumour-cell nuclei for PR positivity and below 1% for negativity; ER-low positive is an ER-specific reporting category.

HR-positive is commonly used for ER-positive, PR-positive or both. Preserve the individual results: ER-positive/PR-negative is not hormone-receptor-negative or triple-negative. PR is primarily prognostic within ER-positive invasive disease. An unusual ER-negative/PR-positive combination should prompt review of the ER stain and controls, not an automatic inference about eligibility for endocrine treatment or a CDK4/6 inhibitor.

notes: PR can bind progesterone and regulate gene programmes, but finding protein in a stained nucleus is not a direct readout of all receptor activity. The ASCO/CAP guideline uses ER to predict potential endocrine benefit and describes PR chiefly as prognostic in ER-positive invasive cancer. A prognostic association and evidence of added benefit from a particular medicine are different questions.

Start with the identified tissue/lesion and invasive tumour-cell nuclei, then the validated stain, percentage, intensity, controls and final PR interpretation read beside ER. Sections are consumed by the assay. Record the specimen/block and context; preservation problems, scant assessable tumour or failed controls can limit interpretation. Percentage, intensity and composite IHC scores have different units. In-situ testing is a separate context, and no tissue-staining percentage is an individual recurrence or benefit probability.

In a fictional adequately controlled report, ER is 80% and PR is below 1%. The invasive cancer is ER-positive and PR-negative; PR does not cancel ER and the pair is not TNBC. These measurements do not alone choose a drug, quantify benefit or prescribe progesterone. Read each observation before asking the separate treatment question.

records.name: Randomised trial
records.tldr: A study that assigns eligible participants to interventions by chance. This reduces treatment-selection bias but does not guarantee identical groups, flawless follow-up or benefit.
records.summary: A randomized trial assigns eligible consenting participants to interventions by chance. Concealing the next assignment protects enrolment against foreknowledge; blinding concerns awareness after assignment. These are different design features. Randomization reduces treatment-selection confounding but leaves possible chance imbalance, missing outcomes and limits on applicability. The comparator, endpoint, analysis and conduct determine what the comparison establishes.

notes: Concealed chance assignment is different from predictable alternation between A and B. Allocation concealment hides the next assignment during enrolment; blinding concerns who knows the assigned treatment afterwards and may not be feasible for every intervention. Report sequence generation, allocation, who was blinded, assigned-group analyses, exclusions, dropout, missing assessments, treatment changes and unequal follow-up. Chance can balance measured and unmeasured factors on average without guaranteeing identical groups in one trial. Random assignment is not random sampling from a population: consenting eligible volunteers remain selected.

Controls can be standard care, standard care plus placebo or another protocol-defined option, not automatically no treatment. A fictional single-group Drug A study showing shrinkage supports an activity question for further study; it does not isolate added survival benefit from selection, natural history and other care. A randomized A-plus-usual-care versus usual-care comparison can test the added effect under sound conduct and analysis, while a volunteer cannot choose their randomized assignment or be promised benefit. A chance-assigned two-group phase 2 trial is randomized even though it is not phase 3.

records.name: Systemic versus local therapy
records.tldr: Local and regional treatments act in selected anatomical areas; systemic treatments circulate more broadly. The route does not guarantee adequate exposure or cancer control at every site.
records.summary:
Surgery, ablation and external radiation address defined tissues, while systemically administered medicines and radiopharmaceuticals distribute more broadly. Regional delivery has an intermediate anatomical scope. Distribution, effective exposure and benefit are separate questions; neither local nor systemic is a guarantee of complete cellular coverage.

Local control, distant progression, progression-free survival, overall survival and symptom relief should be measured separately. A null added-survival comparison does not make palliation irrelevant, and a controlled treated site does not establish control throughout the body. Compare the actual complete strategies rather than assuming that adding a local method always improves outcomes.

records.name: T cell
records.tldr: T cells are immune cells with different recognition systems and roles. Their presence does not by itself show that they recognise or kill cancer.
records.summary: T cells develop through the thymus. Conventional alpha-beta T cells recognise peptide-HLA displays through a paired receptor; CD4 and CD8 identify major co-receptor populations, rather than fixed helper and killer jobs. Some human bladder-tumour CD4 cells showed class-II-dependent cytotoxicity in controlled experiments, while regulatory populations restrain responses. Identity, receptor specificity, state and measured function need separate evidence. A CD3 or CD8 stain establishes a sampled population under a defined panel, not tumour recognition or killing. Report compartment, viable-cell denominator, marker panel and timing. Controlled recognition and target-cell-death assays address different claims; cytokine production, division and treatment benefit are also separate outcomes.
